[[Wikipedia:Intelligent Input Bus|IBus]] (''Intelligent Input Bus'') is an [[Input method#Input method framework|input method framework]], a type of application that allows for easily switching between different keyboard layouts. When combined with an [[input method editor]], it also allows for typing non-Latin characters using a keyboard that does not natively support them.

== Installation ==

[[Install]] the {{Pkg|ibus}} package.

Additionally, see [[Input method#List of available input method editors]] for a comprehensive list of available input method editors.

{{Note|[[GNOME]] has [https://help.gnome.org/misc/release-notes/3.6/i18n-ibus.html.en integrated] IBus since version 3.6 and makes use of it by default, so if you use it as your [[desktop environment]], you may skip [[#Integration]] and go straight to [[#Configuration]].}}

== Integration ==

Set [https://github.com/ibus/ibus/blob/7b014b587259531c2793778c73111e0e61b6c157/setup/main.py#L610 the following] [[environment variables]]:

For Wayland sessions:

 GTK_IM_MODULE=wayland
 XMODIFIERS=@im=ibus
 QT_IM_MODULES=wayland;ibus
 QT_IM_MODULE=ibus

For X11 sessions:

 GTK_IM_MODULE=ibus
 XMODIFIERS=@im=ibus
 QT_IM_MODULE=ibus

To launch IBus on user login, create an [[autostart]] entry with the following command:

 ibus start

Add the {{ic|--type wayland}} flag when used on with [[Wayland compositor]]. On the next login IBus will start along with the user session.

{{Tip|
* The {{AUR|ibus-autostart}} package provides an [[autostart]] entry that can auto start this.
* The {{AUR|ibus-daemon}} package provides an {{ic|ibus@$DISPLAY.service}} that can be [[enable]]d to achieve this.
* [[KDE]] comes with a plasmoid called Input Method Panel that can act as an IBus frontend and can possibly provide a better integrated experience. 
** To launch IBus with Input Method Panel, use the {{ic|1=--panel=/usr/lib/kimpanel-ibus-panel}} option with the ''ibus-daemon'' command above (if the panel does not appear, you can try the {{ic|1=--desktop=kde}} option instead). To configure the ''Input Method Panel'' widget, see the [https://userbase.kde.org/Tutorials/Kimpanel KDE UserBase Wiki] and [[KDE#Widgets]] for details.
** The {{AUR|ibus-autostart-kimpanel}} package provides an [[autostart]] entry that can auto start this.
}}

== Configuration ==

See [[Locale]] for help with adding non-Latin language support to your system.

See [[Fonts#Non-latin scripts]] for a non-exhaustive list of available non-Latin fonts.

=== GNOME ===

[[GNOME]] uses IBus by default, so you can simply go to ''Settings > Keyboard > Input Sources'' and add a keyboard layout for the language of your choice.
	
Some non-Latin languages (e.g. Simplified Chinese) need to enable the ''Show Extended Input Sources'' option in [https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gnome-tweaks GNOME Tweaks].

=== Other desktop environments ===

{{Tip| For [[Wayland]] environments see: [https://github.com/ibus/ibus/wiki/WaylandDesktop WaylandDesktop] }}

To launch the IBus preferences window, you can:

* Right-click on its tray icon and select ''Preferences'', or
* Find and launch the GUI application IBus Preferences, or
* Run the command {{ic|ibus-setup}} in a terminal

The points of interest here are the keyboard shortcut for ''Next input method'' (which is the one you will want to use instead of the default shortcut provided by your desktop environment) and the ''Input Method'' tab where you can add or remove the different keyboard layouts (which is where you will want to do this instead of your desktop environment's default layout manager).

== Tips and tricks ==

=== Emoji input ===

IBus supports the input of emoji icons. Type {{ic|Super+.}} and you will see the input prompt change to an underlined <u>'''e'''</u> character. You can then type the symbol or name of the emoji you want (e.g. ''':)''' or '''face''') and press {{ic|Space}} to render it. If you are satisfied with the result press {{ic|Enter}} to submit it and exit emoji input mode, or press {{ic|Space}} for a second time to open a dialog where you can further customize your desired emoji.

See {{man|7|ibus-emoji}} for more information.

=== Unicode input ===

IBus supports the input of complex Unicode characters. Type {{ic|Ctrl+Shift+u}} and you will see the input prompt change to an underlined <u>'''u'''</u> character. You can then type the code of the Unicode character you want and press {{ic|Space}} or {{ic|Enter}} to render and submit it.

=== Tray icon color ===

By default, IBus uses a dark blue color to display the language symbol of the currently active layout (e.g. '''EN'''). The color value is stored in a [[GNOME#Configuration|gsettings schema]], so if you wish to change it you can run the following command:

 $ gsettings set org.freedesktop.ibus.panel xkb-icon-rgba 'COLOR'

The string {{ic|COLOR}} should conform to the following guidelines:

The RGBA value can be:

# a color name from X11,
# a hex value in form {{ic|#rrggbb}} where {{ic|r}}, {{ic|g}} and {{ic|b}} are hex digits of the red, green, and blue,
# a RGB color in form {{ic|rgb(r,g,b)}} or
# a RGBA color in form {{ic|rgba(r,g,b,a)}} where {{ic|r}}, {{ic|g}} and {{ic|b}} are either integers in the range 0 to 255 or percentage values in the range 0% to 100%, and {{ic|a}} is a floating point value in the range 0 to 1 of the alpha.

{{Tip|You can also use {{Pkg|dconf-editor}} to edit the gsettings schema in a more user-friendly way.}}

{{Note|This does not apply to either [[GNOME]], or [[KDE]] with KDE Input Method Panel, because they both provide their own icons for IBus.}}

=== Layout switcher display delay ===

When pressing the '''Next input method''' hotkey, IBus displays a small dialog to signify the layout switch. By default this dialog is displayed 400ms after pressing the key, but this value can be changed by the user, with some interesting choices being '0' to display the dialog immediately without any delay, or a negative value (e.g. '-1') to switch the layouts without showing the window at all (which may be useful if you only use two layouts and simply switch from one to the other).

The value is stored in a [[GNOME#Configuration|gsettings schema]], so if you wish to change it you can run the following command:

 $ gsettings set org.freedesktop.ibus.general switcher-delay-time 'VALUE'

To show the currently stored value, run the following command:

 $ gsettings get org.freedesktop.ibus.general switcher-delay-time

The string 'VALUE' should conform to the following guidelines:

Set popup delay milliseconds to show IME switcher window. The default is 400.

* 0 = Show the window immediately.
* 0 < Delay milliseconds.
* 0 > Do not show the window and switch prev/next engines.

{{Tip|You can also use {{Pkg|dconf-editor}} to edit the gsettings schema in a more user-friendly way.}}

=== Using modifier key combinations to switch layouts ===

For some reason, the IBus preferences GUI will not let you use a subset of modifier key combinations (e.g. {{ic|Alt+Shift_R}}) as the layout switching hotkey. However, IBus stores the hotkey as a string in a [[GNOME#Configuration|gsettings schema]], so you can still use such combinations by directly editing that string:

 $ gsettings set org.freedesktop.ibus.general.hotkey triggers "['VALUE']"

The string {{ic|'VALUE'}} should be any valid modifier key combination written in a format that IBus recognizes, e.g. {{ic|<Alt>Shift_R}}.

{{Tip|You can also use {{Pkg|dconf-editor}} to edit the gsettings schema in a more user-friendly way.}}

=== rxvt-unicode ===

For ''rxvt-unicode'' to work correctly with IBus, you may need to add the following lines to {{ic|~/.Xresources}}:

 URxvt.inputMethod: ibus
 URxvt.preeditType: OverTheSpot

== Troubleshooting ==

=== Missing packages due to pyenv ===

If using {{ic|pyenv}} to manage python versions and configuration, {{ic|ibus}} dependencies may not be installed on the set global python version. This can happen if the global version is not the one managed by the system (to which dependencies that ibus depends on, such as {{ic|gi}} are installed). This may result in a running but non-functional ibus setup (ibus is in the system tray, but preferences can not be opened, etc). One way to verify this issue is to attempt to run {{ic|ibus-setup}} and see if any missing dependency errors arise.

To fix this issue, change your pyenv global version to the system version:

 pyenv global system

=== Settings removed after restart ===

If you find your settings are being removed consistently after restart (input methods being reverted), you can confirm the engines set to be preloaded and the order in which they will be loaded:

 $ gsettings get org.freedesktop.ibus.general preload-engines
 ['xkb:us::eng']
 $ gsettings get org.freedesktop.ibus.general engines-order
 ['xkb:us::eng', 'anthy']

To ensure {{ic|anthy}} gets loaded in this case, add it to the {{ic|org.freedesktop.ibus.preload-engines}} list:

 $ gsettings set org.freedesktop.ibus.general preload-engines "['xkb:us::eng', 'anthy']"

Changes your changes should be reflected immediately, and should persist across restarts.

=== Ibus IME packages only input keyboard's native charset ===

A possible fix is to set the GTK_IM_MODULE [[environment variable]] to xim instead of ibus: 

{{hc|/etc/environment|2=
GTK_IM_MODULE=xim
QT_IM_MODULE=ibus
XMODIFIERS=@im=ibus
}}

=== Keys "stick" after being held down ===

In certain games, especially those running via Proton, keeping a key pressed for several seconds might result in that key "sticking" (continuing to be registered as pressed) until it is pressed and released again. Limited testing [https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton/issues/5294#issuecomment-1455434318] has found that simply killing the IBus daemon is sufficient to resolve the issue.
